shown.message:
PR #9 is merged, so `main` now holds the paper with the live DSPy check (C8). I opened PR #10 from `main` into `final`, and it's waiting for `internal-review-repo`. Merging that PR into `final` releases the world.

- **Merge:** `figtab-repo` approved #9 at `97f7108`. After that I pushed one change, to the Table 3 caption (`61102f1`), and `figtab-repo` re-approved at that head. `experiment-repo`'s approval of #9 was at the older head `eb6e5cb`, so it was dismissed as stale. It had said the one wording point wasn't blocking, and I made that fix in `97f7108`. The merge went through anyway. The `final` PR is built from `main` at `e71e837`.
- **Build:** the system build of `dev` at `61102f1` is 19 pages, and the main text ends before the references on page 9. The `main` build hadn't appeared yet when I looked, so the PR's built-from check is still to come.
- **Review items from version 1:** the two must-fix items are done. The real-tool check is in the paper with its verdict reported as computed ("not consistent"). The compute figures in checklist item 8 match the README (311.7 CPU-hours charged).
- **Optional review items:** I haven't acted on the optional items R3–R7, and the PR body only says I'll answer them there. "Within 6%" matches the measured ratios (0.95–1.06 up to 100 items), so I left it. I didn't add the White reality-check and Dodge et al. citations because I can't verify them from here. The Fig 1 label overlap belongs to `figtab-repo`.

When `internal-review-repo` reviews #10, I'll merge it if approved. If it asks for changes, I'll address them there.
